candidates.statement: Use online grocery shopping when the week is busy and there is no time to go to the store, or when buying the usual regular stock that does not need exploration.

evidence_candidates.quote: if I have like, a really busy week, and I don't have time to physically go or if I'm just buying the same things that I always buy and like don't need to explore

candidates.statement: Select the store first (Whole Foods) so that items unavailable at that store are not added and do not have to be refiltered later.
context: search on Amazon before selecting Whole Foods

evidence_candidates.quote: sometimes I'll forget to select whole foods. and I'll have to like kind of go back and refilter that

candidates.statement: Order regular grocery items only through the search bar, typing exactly what is wanted, without browsing.
context: regular items with known brand and item

evidence_candidates.quote: But for me it's just like the search bar, and that's it.

candidates.statement: Make the Whole Foods availability marker clearly visible so that it is not easy to miss which items are available at the selected store.
candidates.modality: complaint about low visibility; no explicit request

evidence_candidates.quote: there's like a whole foods icon that appears under the ones that like are actually available in whole foods. But it's not like that visible. So like, it's easy to miss.

candidates.statement: Look at all past orders and produce a grocery list for the user automatically.
context: using the user's own order history

evidence_candidates.quote: it would be cool if they could look at all of my past orders, and like come up with a grocery list for me

candidates.statement: Figuring out exactly what is needed for a month or two weeks is the difficult part of the process.

evidence_candidates.quote: I feel like that part is more what's difficult, like figuring out exactly what I need for a month or 2 weeks.

candidates.statement: Have a template grocery list that can be reused each time and customized for different occasions, such as a weekly list versus a party-planning list.

evidence_candidates.quote: it would be nice like if they could have almost a template grocery list that I could just like reuse every time that I customize, like my weekly grocery list versus my like party planning grocery list

candidates.statement: Check brand, quantity, price and ingredients when buying; quantity is hard to judge online from the fine print and ingredient lists are not always available.

evidence_candidates.quote: It's not as intuitive when you're shopping online, because you kind of have to like. Read the fine print to see if you're getting like one bag of cat litter, or like 10
I'll have to see if they have an ingredient list available which I'm not entirely sure they always do

candidates.statement: Recommend products in a feed while the user scrolls through a category such as snacks.
candidates.modality: 'it would kind of be interesting if'
context: exploring a category of items, e.g. snacks

evidence_candidates.quote: it would kind of be interesting if they like made it when I'm scrolling through like more of, or they probably do this on the back end. But like a Facebook news feed where it's like recommending things.

candidates.statement: Keep online grocery shopping efficient: do not spend time randomly exploring grocery items on the computer.

evidence_candidates.quote: I'm really there for efficiency. I'm not there to look around.

candidates.statement: Prefer to explore groceries in a physical store rather than online.

evidence_candidates.quote: I think personally, I prefer exploring in a physical grocery store if I have to do that.

candidates.statement: For out-of-stock items, choose between a self-picked alternative, the closest alternative picked by the store associate, or no replacement at all.
candidates.modality: reports existing capability; 'it kind of depends on the item'

evidence_candidates.quote: they'll have a an option to select either an alternative that you can pick, or the closest alternative that the store associate will pick, or just like not get it at all

candidates.statement: Do not let a specific or expensive ingredient be replaced by a different item, such as replacing fish sauce with soy sauce.

evidence_candidates.quote: I wouldn't want them to replace the fish sauce with soy sauce, because, like my recipe didn't need that.

candidates.statement: Use in-person pickup rather than delivery because pickup is the balance of saving shipping cost and saving time.

evidence_candidates.quote: I typically like picking it up. because I think it's like the perfect balance of cost saving, since I don't have to pay for shipping, but also time saving

candidates.statement: Understand how the purchase data shared between the in-store and online channels is used.
context: data linking Whole Foods store purchases and online purchases

evidence_candidates.quote: I've been curious like, how do they use that kind of information?

candidates.statement: Privacy concern about the data sharing between the physical store and the online store.
candidates.modality: 'I've always wondered about the privacy concerns'

evidence_candidates.quote: there's a lot of, I guess data sharing between like a physical place that I buy things and an online place

candidates.statement: Every two weeks, show the grocery list for sign-off and then place the order so the user can pick it up.

evidence_candidates.quote: it would be interesting if they had like a way to every 2 weeks. They show you like, okay, here's your grocery list.
once you sign off on it. I'm going to place this order, and then you can go pick it up.

candidates.statement: Create templates of a grocery list and reuse them, and keep using subscriptions for individual items.
candidates.modality: 'I'm kind of repeating myself'; same wish restated
context: already uses Amazon subscriptions for individual items

evidence_candidates.quote: I'm kind of repeating myself, but the ability to create templates of a grocery list. and then just like Reuse

candidates.statement: Find a way to suggest features that might be useful to the user, based on how the user is using the platform.

evidence_candidates.quote: they should just like somehow find a way to suggest features that might be useful to me, based on how I'm using this platform.

candidates.statement: Existing features such as Buy again and lists should not be buried and should be intuitive to find.
context: interface resembles the full Amazon store

evidence_candidates.quote: because the interface is so overwhelming like I haven't even. It wasn't like intuitive to click on. Buy again.

candidates.statement: Reduce the typing and clicking by opening one list and reading through it instead of reconstructing the list every time.

evidence_candidates.quote: the biggest overhaul would probably be, I just like click on one list and read through it rather than like having to reconstruct the list every time. So I think it would like reduce the amount of typing and clicking

candidates.statement: Make the list more comprehensive so that forgotten items do not force a physical trip to the store.
candidates.modality: 'I think it would ... also be more comprehensive'

evidence_candidates.quote: and also be more comprehensive, because sometimes I just like, forget things
I forgot one item, and then I'll have to like physically. Go into the store for that.
